judged_text: The members endpoint accepts an unbounded, unvalidated user-controlled limit parameter ((params[:limit] || 50).to_i with no upper cap) and performs a full group.users.count on every request. An anonymous client (this is the public /groups/:group_id/members.json route, gated only by ensure_can_see!) can pass limit=2000000000 to make the serializer iterate every member of a large group, and hammer the endpoint to force a COUNT(*) over a large join table per request — a cheap amplification/DoS vector against any site with large groups; the old code capped automatic groups at 200.

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the new code sets `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and applies it directly to `group.users...limit(limit)` with no upper bound, so a client can request an extremely large `limit` and force the server to fetch/serialize up to the entire group membership. The same method now also performs `total = group.users.count` on every request, adding a potentially expensive `COUNT(*)` over the group-users relation per hit. Both behaviors are visible in the diff and create a plausible public DoS/amplification vector on `/groups/:group_id/members.json`.
